results.summary:
Track #217 ran as four nodes in three waves, then the root's own pass. A profile can now declare a capability map — an intent from a closed vocabulary bound to what this harness calls it — and the grant that binding needs is derived rather than typed twice.

What each node landed:
- #255 (PR #263) — `effectiveTools(profile, task, board) -> {tools, dropped}` in src/model.js, the one derivation of a launch's tool list. A card narrows, never widens; drops recorded. src/dispatch.js stopped reading allowed_tools. No new config, no behaviour change: the seam alone, so this feature and the tool posture (#223) plug into one function.
- #259 (PR #264) — frozen CAPABILITIES vocabulary (review, goal, specify) with a per-intent meaning, `capabilityCommand(profile, intent)`, and loadBoard validation of an optional `profile.capabilities`.
- #260 (PR #267) — the worker brief names the bound command for each intent a card triggers (`briefIntents`/`capabilityLine`, src/context.js); an unmapped intent renders nothing.
- #261 (PR #269) — the implied grant derived INSIDE effectiveTools (`capabilityGrants` -> `grantWithCapabilities`, one consumer), doctor's `capability map` check, and the /kanban:operate review row using the declared capability. Settled there: #114's `kb.skills` grant is not subsumed (its source is a card field, not a profile binding) and stays.

The root's pass (PR #271, branch kb/217 = kb/260 merged with kb/261): docs/wiki/features/capability-map.md describing the feature as one thing, the glossary terms (capability map, binding, intent), the page-plan entry and the log.md line.

Verified for real, not taken on report:
- Bound {"review": "/code-review", "goal": "/goal"} on this board's claude profile. `hkb doctor` gained exactly two lines (the map printed, and "every binding is one its launch can grant"); `hkb context 260` gained exactly one; unbinding restored both byte for byte.
- The derivation is real and harness-scoped: a claude-shaped profile granting ["Read","Bash"] plus a `review` binding yields ["Read","Bash","Skill"]; the same binding on a copilot launch yields ["Read"]; unbound returns the profile's own array untouched. (The shipped claude profile already carries Skill, so it alone would not have proved anything.)
- Every derived grant goes through effectiveTools: capabilityGrants has exactly one consumer, and src/doctor.js asks that function rather than recomputing.
- lint clean, 1087/1087 tests, smoke passes on the merged whole. wiki-check reports both capability pages fresh; its 15 stale pages all predate this track, verified by comparing each page's covers SHAs against origin/main blobs — zero newly stale.

Gaps found and filed rather than silently fixed:
- #272 — a card narrowing kb.tools can strip a capability's derived grant (widening happens before narrowing) while the brief still names the command the launch now denies; `dropped` stays empty because it records only what the card asked for and did not get. #114's drift returning through the card.
- #273 — trackFanout (src/track.js) and the Stop hook (src/hook.js) still read allowed_tools raw. Neither builds a launch so neither breaks the "one derivation" rule as written, but trackFanout has a live failure mode: a card narrowing Agent away still gets the fan-out brief.
- Not filed, documented as a design limit: the drift guarantee is Claude-only — one invocation shape is known (a /-command on a claude launch implies Skill), so a binding on another harness implies no tool.

Still open: the four node PRs (#263 -> main, #264 -> kb/255, #267 -> kb/259, #269 -> kb/259) and the track PR #271 -> main, which contains all of them. Merging #271 lands the whole track; the node PRs are the per-node checkpoints. Nothing merged — this board's dispatch.merge.mode is "operator", so the click is the human's.

residual_risk: #272 and #273 (both already filed, both in triage) remain open: a card narrowing kb.tools can strip a capability's derived grant with no record in `dropped`, and trackFanout/the Stop hook still read allowed_tools raw rather than through effectiveTools. Precedence/design calls the design record explicitly reserved for a human.

The drift guarantee (capabilityTool) is Claude-only -- a binding on a Copilot or Codex launch implies no tool grant, which is honest but means doctor can only prove agreement where hkb knows the invocation shape.
15 wiki pages elsewhere in docs/wiki/ are stale from unrelated work across the repo's history; left untouched as out of this track's scope.

results.summary:
Root/verify pass for track #217, continuing PR #271 (kb/217). All three children (#255, #259, #260, #261) are closed and their work is already on this branch. This attempt's own contribution: merged origin/main (which had moved with #254's MCP-approval-diagnosis commit) resolving two small conflicts (an import list in src/doctor.js, one page-plan entry in docs/wiki/wiki.config.yml — kept both sides in each case), then verified the whole feature end to end on this repo's own board.

What I actually saw running it for real: with `.kanban/board.json`'s `claude` profile temporarily given `"capabilities": {"review": "/code-review", "goal": "/goal"}`, `hkb doctor` gained exactly two lines (`capability map — 2 bound: claude: review -> /code-review (Skill) - claude: goal -> /goal (Skill)` and `every binding is one its launch can grant`), and `hkb context 260` gained exactly one line after the Acceptance criteria heading (`On this harness that is /goal - state the outcome a piece of work is for, so a worker can tell done from finished`). Reverting the binding restored both outputs byte for byte, and `git diff` on .kanban/board.json confirmed no residual change — this is the byte-identical promise, verified across all three children's work in one place, not just per-child in isolation.

Checked the vocabulary and derivation agree: CAPABILITIES in src/model.js (review/goal/specify) matches what both wiki pages and skills/kanban/SKILL.md's operate review row describe. Confirmed effectiveTools is the only place a derived grant is computed (capabilityGrants -> grantWithCapabilities, single caller; hkb doctor's capability map check asks effectiveTools rather than recomputing) by reading src/model.js and src/doctor.js directly — nothing else in the merged tree calls capabilityGrants.

Wiki: docs/wiki/features/capability-map.md (the whole-feature page, already written in attempt 1) and docs/wiki/concepts/capability-portability.md (the contract page from #261) both needed only a restamp after the main-merge touched src/model.js and src/doctor.js for unrelated reasons (#254's MCP diagnosis) -- confirmed via `git log` that no capability-related lines changed in that range. Ran wiki-stamp.mjs on both; wiki-check.mjs now reports both fresh. docs/wiki/log.md already carries the track's summary line from attempt 1 -- no new entry needed.

Gaps found and NOT fixed, per the brief -- both already filed as their own triage cards from attempt 2's review, so no new cards needed: #272 (a card narrowing kb.tools can silently strip a capability's derived grant -- the loss isn't recorded in `dropped`) and #273 (trackFanout in src/track.js and the Stop hook in src/hook.js still read profile.allowed_tools raw instead of going through effectiveTools, so neither sees a card's narrowing or a derived grant). Both are precedence/design decisions the design record itself said were not this card's call.

Verification: npm run lint clean; npm test 1099/1099 pass; npm run smoke passes (packs, installs, runs the tarball). Pushed the merge + restamp to kb/217 (PR #271, still `Closes #217`, base main) -- gh api confirms PR is now MERGEABLE (was CONFLICTING) and a `test` GitHub Actions run started on the new push (run 33576552434, in_progress) -- CI is not silently absent.
